title: Wait for every worker with one semaphore

blocks.text: A semaphore's permits belong to nobody: **any thread** may `release()`, and a `release()` that comes **before** any `acquire()` is not lost, it simply raises the count. The page's start gate uses `new Semaphore(0)`, and its edge cases note that the count may even start **below zero**: `new Semaphore(-2)` needs two releases before one acquire can succeed.
Write `Rendezvous`, which lets a coordinator wait until `workers` workers have each reported ready, using one `Semaphore`:

items: `void ready()` is called once by each worker, from any thread, at any time, even before the coordinator waits.
`boolean awaitAll(long timeout, TimeUnit unit)` waits **at most** `timeout` for every worker to be ready, and returns whether they all were.

rows: three threads each call `ready()`; then `awaitAll(1, SECONDS)`
a coordinator waits in `awaitAll(8, SECONDS)`; two other threads call `ready()`

cases.says: When every worker has called ready, from its own thread and before anyone waits, awaitAll returns true.
awaitAll returns false while even one worker has not called ready, and true once the last one has.
With no worker ready, awaitAll gives up after its timeout and returns false.
A coordinator already waiting in awaitAll is woken when the last worker calls ready.
A timeout of 250,000 microseconds or 1,600 ms waits that long in full: the unit is honoured and nothing is rounded to whole seconds.

concepts: Any thread may release a permit, and a release that comes before any acquire is kept, which makes a semaphore a signal between threads.
A semaphore may start at zero or below, so acquirers wait until enough releases have brought the count above zero.
